title: How much line does an isometric cube use?
description: A cube two units on every side is drawn on an isometric grid. The board counts the nine visible edges, finds the length of each edge, and multiplies to get the units of line. Keeko's doubt is that all twelve edges are drawn.
teaching_notes: One idea: a cube drawn from a corner shows nine edges, three in each direction, and the hidden edges add no line. Watch for students who count all twelve edges.

source: Draw a 2 by 2 by 2 cube on an isometric grid. How many units
video_script.why: The child counts the visible edges of an isometric cube and finds the units of line they use.
video_script.substitution: Units of line = number of visible edges x length of each edge.
video_script.anchor: a cube two units on every side, drawn on an isometric grid with its three hidden edges dotted at the back
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks all twelve edges are drawn, so the cube needs twenty four units. Three edges are hidden at the back, so only nine are drawn, and nine times two is eighteen.
video_script.payoff_line: The cube uses eighteen units of line over nine visible edges

final_answer.value: 18 units of line over 9 visible edges
final_answer.spoken: eighteen units of line over nine visible edges

hold_back: Answer: 18 units of line over 9 visible edges
maths_rules: a cube seen from a corner shows 3 faces and 9 edges: 3 along height, 3 along length, 3 along depth
check by directions: 3 x 2 = 6 for each direction, 6 + 6 + 6 = 18
slip: 12 x 2 = 24 counts the 3 hidden edges as well
video_script.design: The cube drawn on an isometric grid on the stage. Edges are traced in three passes, one direction at a time, and the three hidden edges are shown dotted at the back.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about drawing a cube.
<bookmark mark='cube'/>Draw a cube that is two units long, two units deep and two units tall.
<bookmark mark='grid'/>Draw it on a grid called an isometric grid.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many units of line do its visible edges use?

beats.on_screen: the cube on the isometric grid stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the isometric grid with lines in three directions; the cube seen from a corner with three faces; three hidden edges dotted at the back

marks.dirs: the three directions of the grid are marked height, length and depth
marks.seen: the cube is seen from a corner and three faces are tinted
marks.hid: three edges at the back are dotted

narration: <bookmark mark='dirs'/>An isometric grid has lines in three directions, for height, length and depth.
<bookmark mark='seen'/>Seen from a corner, a cube shows three faces and nine edges.
<bookmark mark='hid'/>The other three edges are hidden at the back.

beats.on_screen: Given: a cube 2 units long, 2 units deep and 2 units tall, drawn on an isometric grid

marks.given: the three lengths of the cube are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a cube is two units long, two units deep and two units tall.

beats.on_screen: To find: the units of line used by the visible edges

marks.find: the words units of line are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the units of line used by the visible edges.

beats.on_screen: Visible edges: 3 along height, 3 along length, 3 along depth, so 9 edges

marks.count: the visible edges are counted in three groups of three and 9 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='count'/>Step one, count the visible edges. There are nine, three in each direction.

beats.on_screen: Each edge of this cube is 2 units long

marks.len: one edge is marked with a length of 2 units

narration: <bookmark mark='len'/>Step two, find the length of each edge. Each edge of this cube is two units long.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Step three, multiply. Nine edges of two units each use nine times two, which is eighteen units.

beats.on_screen: Check by directions: 3 x 2 = 6 for each direction, 6 + 6 + 6 = 18

marks.dir: each direction is tinted in turn and 3 x 2 = 6 is written beside it

narration: <bookmark mark='dir'/>Step four, check by directions. Each direction has three edges of two units, which is six units.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Six plus six plus six makes eighteen, as before.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 18 units of line over 9 visible edges
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The cube uses eighteen units of line over nine visible edges.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the isometric cube
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 12 x 2 = 24; the three dotted edges at the back are highlighted; the bubble is struck through

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows all the edges of the cube drawn in full
marks.hid: the three dotted edges at the back glow

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks all twelve edges are drawn, so the cube needs twenty four units.
<bookmark mark='hid'/>But three edges are hidden at the back, and we draw only what we can see.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Nine edges are visible, and nine times two is eighteen.
